newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower on mild weather.

text.p: Private forecasts for frost-free weather in the U.S. Midwest over the next seven to 10 days pressured CBOT soybean futures to a mostly lower close, traders said.

"The trade still doesn't know the crop size on corn and beans. That's up to Mother Nature and we're spitting in the dark plus it all comes down to frost," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Trading remained volatile amid the uncertain outcome of this year's U.S. soybean crop with fund long liquidation, profit taking and a technical slide hitting prices, they said.
Rain was expected to move across the U.S. Midwest Thursday and Friday bringing cool weekend weather but forecasters disagreed on whether temperatures would warm early next week.
"The U.S. and European models are at odds again," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Grains and soy were hit by increased competition for export business plus news the EU's grain crop in 1996 would total 200.7 million tonnes, up 23 million from last year.
Soybeans closed 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 4-1/2 higher, with November down two at $7.94.

Nearby September closed higher on short covering, the posting of no deliveries on that contract and on position squaring as traders continued to get out of that month before expiration slated for 1201 CDT Thursday.
Traders said the potential existed for volatile trading Thursday going into the midday expiration.
Losses were limited in other months because of the strength in the September and on late commercial buying, they said.

Cargill Inc and Term Commodities each bought four million November in late dealings, they said. Funds sold at least 15.0 million bushels of November, Refco Inc bought nine million November and sold four million and LIT America sold six million bushels of November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, up from 52,270 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, up from 20,386 Wednesday.
